title: I3C SERIAL COMMUNICATIONS SOFT IP CORE USING HLS/AUTO-CODING EXPRO+
description: Objective: To develop an Improved Inter Integrated Circuit (I3C) serial protocol soft IP for the Controller and Target using High Level Synthesis (HLS)/auto-coding techniques.Description: I3C (Improved Inter Integrated Circuits) standard is an evolution of the I2C standard targeting multi IC (Integrated Circuits) serial communications, but it is also seen as a replacement of the legacy protocols (such as SPI, SMBus, UART). I3C improves the performance and addresses the downsides of the communication standards that are encountered in many platforms and payloads to access memory, ADC/DACs or optical transceivers. The advantage of I3C is improved communication speeds and data rates (up to 30Mbps) than its predecessors and reduced power consumption maintaining reliability capabilities. Other advantages include: multicontroller capabilities; push-pull driver with increased radiation robustness; Cyclic Redundancy Check (CRC) for the detection of errors; Lower voltage operation; Multi node capabilities; Still low pin count (2 pins); and includedhot join capabilities. The main goal of the activity is to develop technology independent soft IP cores for the Controller and for the Target, compliant to the MIPI I3C Basic standard (2021) and using HLS/auto-coding as much as possible. The activity develops soft IPs for the I3C Controller and I3C Target as specified in the I3C Basic standard released in 2021. It is aimed to be developed using to a great extent HLS (High Level Synthesis)/auto-coding techniques creating technology independent VHDL for its source code. It is targeted to be implemented in at least two FPGA and one ASIC technologies. It shall also be validated in one European FPGA technology. The soft IP core shall be delivered as a database including sources, requirements, architectural documentation and reports justifying full verification and validation campaigns performed. I3C is selected as the sideband bus protocol for DDR5/onwards memorieschips. This is a key relevance in the future Telecom and/or EOP missions. The product is targeted to expand the ESA portfolio. Thisactivity encompasses the following tasks: - Trade-off on the target technologies, study the hardware needs for such IP and development plan for high level modelling and autocoding approach. - Definition phase - Architectural phase - Development and verification phase - Detailed design and Validation phase - Technology porting phase - IPs delivery
